pairs.subject: production-pipeline-phasing
pairs.evidence: lib/frames/picture/unit.ts:78 Picture units carry their place on the film as startS/holdS seconds, and startS is null (never a guessed 0) when a beat cannot be placed. The Frames phase speaks the shared clock and shows absence on it; around that, human layers are kept, plate renders survive a reload, and the shot gate cannot fake a pass.

techniques.evidence: lib/frames/picture/unit.ts:78 Units are start+hold in film seconds. A unit that cannot be placed has null on the clock, not an invented position.

lib/frames/directionPlan.ts:14 The direction pass lands as a proposal of ops. Any layer a human touched is a conflict whose default is keep, so the expensive pass edits the cut and never silently overwrites human decisions.

lib/frames/shotReview.ts:115 The shot-list/prompt gate before plate spend turns any check that examined nothing into not-engaged. It reports engaged counts and a named NOT_CHECKED list, never a pass by default.

lib/frames/frames.ts:92 An in-flight plate render's idempotency receipt is persisted with the cut. A reload re-issues under the same key and receives the pixels already paid for, instead of buying the render twice.

pairs.subject: production-pipeline-phasing
pairs.evidence: packages/producers/src/research/partJob.ts:75 Every research act is a persisted kernel job, single-flighted per act and unit at enqueue time inside the confirm's transaction. A double click is one purchase, a reload loses nothing, and interrupted stays a live state the operator sees.

techniques.evidence: packages/producers/src/research/partJob.ts:75 Claim-time single-flight. A second confirm of the same act and unit while one is live adopts that job instead of enqueueing a second paid one.

packages/producers/src/research/facts.ts:58 The runtime target is the project's own figure, seeded from the format template's default and null when neither exists. Every part act reads this one target.

packages/producers/src/research/followUp.ts:69 The notebook is a durable asset. A follow-up revises it through allowlisted edit effects (confirms/downgrades/kills/adds) and an unusable answer refuses whole; the notebook is never regenerated or partially applied.

packages/producers/src/research/define.ts:44 An act whose upstream input is not settled is refused at plan time, before any unit is bought (partAct.ts: refusals "applied before the plan, never after").

techniques.evidence: app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/CutClock.tsx:26 The one clock both Score and Cut draw. Each block is startS/durS with ok, missing and drift as first-class states; Score.tsx:157 marks a cue with no active take as missing at its true span.

app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/CutFinish.tsx:100 The expensive render is gated by finish checks: a blocking fail replaces the render button with a blocked chip carrying the deny sentences. The music bed reads unmeasured, never a fail, when no take exists.
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Render.tsx:7 The render is a kernel job behind a receipt and its progress is the job's state, replacing v1's elapsed clock over one blocking request.
app/(studio)/projects/[id]/[part]/_edit/Takes.tsx:34 A shot counts as ready only when a person has adopted a take. Generated takes are candidates until then, so the asset boundary is the human act.
